display_title: HORIZON-CL5-2027-01-D1-13 Next generation scenarios for informing climate and sustainability transitions – Horizon Europe
call_module_title: HORIZON-CL5-2027-01-D1-13 Next generation scenarios for informing climate and sustainability transitions
executive_summary: Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action that funds improved Integrated Assessment Models (models combining economy, energy, land use and climate) or alternative approaches for next-generation climate scenarios, in one of three areas: A, integrating climate impacts and adaptation into mitigation pathways; B, improved scenario frameworks extending the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways; C, more detailed representation of mitigation and adaptation policies. Consortia must include at least three independent entities from three different low or lower/upper-middle-income countries and relevant social sciences and humanities expertise; new models and tools must be open access. Funded as a lump sum at up to 100%; indicative topic budget EUR 24 million, around EUR 4 million per project, with at least two projects per area. Opened 17 November 2026; single-stage deadline 4 March 2027.
status_rationale: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027 Part 8 (Climate, Energy and Mobility), pp. 80–84, Specific conditions, Expected Outcome and Scope of HORIZON-CL5-2027-01-D1-13, funds research to improve global Integrated Assessment Models and climate scenario frameworks that inform IPCC-type assessments and climate policy. It does not touch TenneT's field: the work concerns economy-wide, global mitigation and adaptation pathways, not the planning, operation or resilience of the electricity system, and no project file is close to it; Target Grid 2045 and the grid investment plans use energy scenarios, but of a different kind and scale. Both project dates are null because the call states no start, end or duration.
